description: Every dependency is pinned exactly; Renovate bumps the pins. Commit types drive release-please: fix(deps) = runtime (lands in the next release as a patch), chore(deps) = tooling/CI (no release).

lockFileMaintenance.description: Refreshes transitive deps in package-lock.json and docker/requirements.txt. Monthly, and not covered by minimumReleaseAge, so review the lockfile diff for new packages before merging. Runtime-affecting, so fix

customManagers.description: Version pins in the workflow env annotated with `# renovate:` comments (main.yaml and pr.yaml)
Runner labels in the docker-build matrix (runs-on uses ${{ matrix.arch.runner }}, which the github-actions manager can't see)

packageRules.description: Supply-chain delay: don't propose a version until it is 7 days old, so compromised releases are usually caught and pulled first (Shai-Hulud 2.0 versions were still live ~3 days after upload). github-runners has no release timestamps, so it is excluded. Security fixes (vulnerabilityAlerts) bypass this by design; review them by hand
Runtime dependencies (including the tar override, which ships in the image): land in the next release as a patch
Runtime: Docker base image and the yt-dlp lockfile
Dev tooling, GitHub Actions and CI tool pins: no release
Keep the image's Node and the CI NODE_VERSION in one PR so they stay in sync (runtime, so fix)
Stay on Node 22 LTS; Node majors are deliberate, manual upgrades. A regex, because docker versioning cannot parse "<23" and would filter out every 22.x-trixie-slim tag
Move every runner label (direct runs-on and the docker-build matrix) in one PR
engines.node is a compatibility range, not a dependency to pin
